searchText: <@427491045308235776> It seems to me that for the PrecomputedWeights in the ref impl https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/master/polynomial/precomputed_weights.py#L9 we can pick anything for the domain right? In the tests it's [0, 255] that is used (https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/2332ab82a77c17024861eb47fd140301c27de980/multiproof/multiproof_test.py#L32-L33) but we could use the roots of unity so we can reuse the same code as EIP4844 KZG right? i.e. replace https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/master/multiproof/quotient.py#L6-L35 with quotient polynomial eval https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/deneb/polynomial-commitments.md#compute_quotient_eval_within_domain and the same outside the domain. cc <@785811170387951616> ^ > It seems to me that for the PrecomputedWeights in the ref impl https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/master/polynomial/precomputed_weights.py#L9 > we can pick anything for the domain right? Yep the equations are generic over the domain being used, so you can use any domain > In the tests it's [0, 255] that is used (https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/2332ab82a77c17024861eb47fd140301c27de980/multiproof/multiproof_test.py#L32-L33) > but we could use the roots of unity so we can reuse the same code as EIP4844 KZG right? We would not be able to re-use that because the order of the multiplicative subgroup of the scalar field of bandersnatch does not factor into a large enough power of 2, ie it does not have a high enough 2-adicity sage gives: > factor(13108968793781547619861935127046491459309155893440570251786403306729687672800) = 2^5 * 3 * 5^2 * 48407612962807291 * 2038476065687664805409 * 55352597255927763854484663053009063 So best you can get is a subgroup of size 2^5 for 2n'th roots of unity -- 48407612962807291 does form another group but its way too large and even if it was not I'd stick with 2n'th roots of unity given that the domain in question is linked to the width/branhing factor of the verkle trie

excerpts.content:
<@427491045308235776> It seems to me that for the PrecomputedWeights in the ref impl https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/master/polynomial/precomputed_weights.py#L9
we can pick anything for the domain right?

In the tests it's [0, 255] that is used (https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/2332ab82a77c17024861eb47fd140301c27de980/multiproof/multiproof_test.py#L32-L33)
but we could use the roots of unity so we can reuse the same code as EIP4844 KZG right?

i.e. replace https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref/blob/master/multiproof/quotient.py#L6-L35
with quotient polynomial eval
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/deneb/polynomial-commitments.md#compute_quotient_eval_within_domain
and the same outside the domain.

sage gives:

So best you can get is a subgroup of size 2^5 for 2n'th roots of unity -- 48407612962807291 does form another group but its way too large and even if it was not I'd stick with 2n'th roots of unity given that the domain in question is linked to the width/branhing factor of the verkle trie
